items.title: Show HN: Zroar – Serialized Roaring Bitmaps in Zig
items.contentSnippet:
zroar is a ground-up implementation of Roaring Bitmaps data structure in Zig. zroar stores both the keys and (array, bitmap) containers in a single flat byte buffer, making the in-memory representation equal to the on-disk or over-the-network representation, eliminating the serialization/deserialization step entirely.
The design was originally aimed at systems which keep their posting lists on disk, but zroar performs faster than CRoaring even for purely in-memory ops, due to CPU cache locality.

items.title: Nvidia finds that simple linear math can replace costly AI model handoffs
items.contentSnippet:
When an agentic AI system hands a task from a small model to a larger one — or back down again — it pays a steep tax: the receiving model has to recompute the entire conversation from scratch, driving up compute costs and latency. This is a major bottleneck for enterprises building long-horizon, multi-LLM workflows.
To solve this challenge, researchers at Nvidia have introduced a cross-model KV cache transfer technique that directly maps the prefilled KV cache from a source model into the target
